newsitem.title: TAIWAN: High waves halt Taiwan crude port repair.
newsitem.headline: High waves halt Taiwan crude port repair.

text.p: State-owned Chinese Petroleum said on Tuesday turbulent waves prevented repair crews from reopening its troubled north Taiwan crude port, and that an adjacent refinery had crude reserves good for about 20 days.
"Our repair team is still trying to repair the two oil offloading units, but strong currents stopped us," a Taoyuan refinery official told Reuters by telephone.
"The Taoyuan refinery has about 400,000 kilolitres of crude supplies on reserve, enough for about 20 days," he added.

Unspecified pipeline problems shut down both of the Taoyuan port's offshore units on September 15, and engineers have battled foul weather to reopen them. One unit was partially reopened for a short period on September 23.
Chinese Petroleum shut down one of the Taoyuan refinery's two 100,000-barrels-per-day crude units on September 15 due to the cutoff of supplies from the crude port.

Chinese Petroleum issued a tender on Tuesday for 32,000 tonnes of jet fuel for arrival between November 1 to 30, a company official said. Officials declined to say whether the tender was related to the Taoyuan shutdown.
Taiwan's northern and northeastern waters have had dangerously choppy waves in the wake of Typhoon Zane, which passed by the island at the weekend before heading for Japan.
High waves swept more than 10 fishermen into the sea from a pier at Taiwan's northern Keelung port late on Monday, killing at least two of them and sparking a search for others.
